LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
HTML: United Kingdom. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
Who is credited with discovering Moscovium?
Moscovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Who is credited with discovering Oxycodone?
Oxycodone: Martin Freund. It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star is only visible from Earth when its beam of radiation sweeps directly toward us — what's the object?
Pulsar (pulsating star, on the model of quasar) is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle, and fat, this rare cancer of mesenchymal cells makes up just 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones. What is it?
Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from cells of mesenchymal origin.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?
One of the oldest of the natural sciences, it leans on math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything from comets to quasars beyond Earth's atmosphere — what field is this?
Astronomy: Scientific study of celestial objects.
A sessile marine arthropod related to crabs and lobsters, folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety of it — what creature is it?
Barnacle: Subclass of sessile marine crustaceans.
This natural science rests on five big themes — the cell, genes and heredity, evolution, energy transformation, and homeostasis — to explain life itself. What field is it?
A synthetic group-7 transition metal made only in particle accelerators, this radioactive element honors a Danish physicist and sits at atomic number 107 — what is it?
Bohrium: Chemical element with atomic number 107 (Bh)

Known also as the Zambezi or Lake Nicaragua species, this aggressive fish can thrive in both salt and fresh water, having been tracked more than 1,100 kilometers up the Mississippi River — what animal is it?
Bull shark: Species of fish. Bull sharks are listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.
Which compound is the main psychoactive component of cannabis?
Tetrahydrocannabinol is one of 483 known compounds in the plant, and the one responsible for the high. CBD is not psychoactive in the same way.
Also known as an Ovcharka, this large livestock-guardian breed was developed in the Soviet Union around 1920 from mountain and steppe animals of the Caucasus region — which breed?
Caucasian Shepherd Dog: Russian breed of livestock guardian dog. It was bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.
Its roasted root has long served as a coffee substitute, while today its extracted inulin shows up as a sweetener and fiber additive in packaged foods — which blue-flowered plant?
Chicory: Flowering plant in the daisy family.
Sold under the brand name Plavix, this antiplatelet drug taken after a heart attack or coronary stent placement kicks in within two hours and keeps working for five days — what is it?

Clopidogrel: Antiplatelet medication. Clopidogrel, sold under the brand name Plavix among others, is an antiplatelet medication used to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke in those at high risk.
Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Named after the Greek word for 'hedgehog' because of its spiky central disk, this North American daisy relative is nicknamed the coneflower — what is it?
Echinacea: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.
Often triggered by contaminated food, NSAIDs, or autoimmune conditions like coeliac disease, which medical term describes inflammation of the small intestine?
Enteritis: Inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.
This Austrian-German automotive engineer built the first gasoline-electric hybrid car and designed the Volkswagen Beetle, but also contributed tanks to Nazi Germany's war effort — who was he?
Ferdinand Porsche: Austrian-born German automotive engineer, inventor (1875–1951)
Part of the rose family and prized for fruit that ranges from very sweet to notably tart, this genus's garden hybrid is an important commercial crop worldwide — which genus is it?
Found on every continent except Antarctica, these lizards are unusual for making vocal chirps and clicks, and most lack eyelids, relying on a transparent membrane instead — what are they?
Gecko: Lizards belonging to the suborder Gekkota.
One of the very first animals domesticated — in Iran some 10,000 years ago — this Bovidae cousin of the sheep now numbers over 1.1 billion worldwide, 150 million of them in India; what is it?
Also nicknamed the millionfish, this livebearing freshwater fish is one of the world's most popular aquarium species — which fish?
This medical term describes red blood cells rupturing and spilling their contents into the plasma — a process triggered by bacterial toxins or even intense exercise. What is it?
Hemolysis: Rupturing of red blood cells and release of their contents. Hemolysis may occur in vivo or in vitro.

The only birds whose first two neck vertebrae are fused together, these Old World birds have a long down-curved bill sometimes topped with a bony casque, and share an ecological niche with toucans in the Americas — which birds?
Hornbill: Family of birds. The family is omnivorous, feeding on fruit and small animals.
Marked in its severe stage by hallucinations and paradoxical undressing, which condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35 degrees Celsius?
Hypothermia: Human body core temperature below 35 °C (95 °F)
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
With Emmanuelle Charpentier, this Berkeley biochemist proposed in 2012 that CRISPR-Cas9 could edit genomes — work that won them the 2020 Nobel in Chemistry; who is she?
Jennifer Doudna: American biochemist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
A genus of roughly 125 succulent species native mostly to Madagascar, one of its members became one of the first plants ever sent into space, aboard a Soviet resupply mission in 1979 — which genus?
Kalanchoe: Genus of flowering plants in the stonecrop family.
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
Sometimes called the paleomammalian cortex, this set of brain structures — including the amygdala — governs emotion, motivation, and long-term memory — what is it called?
Limbic system: Set of brain structures involved in emotion and motivation. Its various components support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long-term memory, and olfaction.

This German fluid dynamicist built the mathematical foundations of subsonic aerodynamics, identifying the 'boundary layer' and lifting-line theory — and lent his name to a dimensionless number. Who was he?

Despite its fox-like markings, this leggy, reddish-coated canine of the South American savanna is neither a fox nor a close relative of more familiar canines, and it plays a key role dispersing fruit seeds — what is it?

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.
Sold as Versed, this benzodiazepine sedates rather than knocks you out, can be sprayed up the nose or squirted in the cheek, and famously causes anterograde amnesia — which drug?
Midazolam: Benzodiazepine used for anesthesia and procedural sedation.
This rounded mound of fatty tissue overlies the junction where the two pubic bones meet — what is it?
Mons pubis: Rounded mass of fatty tissue found over the pubic symphysis.
Made by giving a paper loop a half-twist before joining the ends, this non-orientable surface first appeared in Roman mosaics — what is it called?
Möbius strip: Non-orientable surface with one edge.
A former director of Russia's FSB who later served as Security Council secretary, this close Putin ally played a key role in the decisions to annex Crimea and invade Ukraine — who is he?
Nikolai Patrushev: Russian politician and security officer (born 1951)

The type species that gives its name to the Oleaceae family of lilac, jasmine, and ash, this Mediterranean evergreen bears a fruit classed botanically as a drupe — like a cherry or peach — what is it?

Though isolated observations date back to the 6th century BC, this science's modern foundation is credited to Georges Cuvier's 1796 work demonstrating that species could go extinct — what field is this?
Paleontology: Study of past life through fossils.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.
This colorless, highly toxic pnictogen hydride is pure when odorless, but technical samples reek of rotting fish — and impurities can make it burst into flame in air — what is it?
Named after a French mathematician and physicist, this materials-science measure captures how much a material bulges sideways when compressed lengthwise — what is it?
Poisson's ratio: Measure of material deformation perpendicular to loading.
Found just below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male-only gland acts like a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation — which organ?
Prostate: Gland of the male reproductive system.
Its thick bark gets harvested every 9 to 12 years for wine-bottle stoppers and cricket-ball cores — what species of oak, native to southwest Europe and Africa, is this?
Quercus suber: Species of plant. Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
In 1948, this Japanese engineer turned a wooden shack producing bicycle motors into a multinational car and motorcycle manufacturer — who is he?
Soichiro Honda: Japanese businessman. Soichiro Honda (本田 宗一郎, Honda Sōichirō; 17 November 1906 – 5 August 1991) was a Japanese engineer and industrialist.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Patented in 1953 and originally derived from Streptomyces bacteria, this antibiotic treats ailments from acne to cholera to plague by blocking bacterial protein production — which drug?
Tetracycline: Antibiotic. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Home to more than 4,200 described species, this family of large crane flies can be identified by the length of their maxillary palps — what is it?
Tipulidae: Family of flies. There are more than 30 genera and 4,200 described species in Tipulidae, common and widespread throughout the world.
Element 74 boasts the highest melting point of any known element — a scorching 3,422 °C — and carries the symbol W from its German name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten: Chemical element with atomic number 74 (W)
Released from the posterior pituitary when body fluids get too concentrated, this hormone helps kidneys reabsorb water and may also influence pair bonding — what is it?
Vasopressin: Mammalian hormone released from the pituitary gland.
Nicknamed the 'cock-of-the-woods,' this ground-dwelling grouse is the largest of all its kind, with males growing to nearly twice the size of females — which bird?
Western capercaillie: Species of bird. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Xenon is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for xenon is Xe. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Bismuth is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for bismuth is Bi. Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
